issues.symptom: Director output-contract exposed user_profile, appetite, non_goals, feasibility_constraints, risks_and_unknowns, and decision_rationale without canonical lock protection.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The fields existed only in markdown and were never added to canonical schema/template/validator contracts.
hypotheses.verification: rg and schema inspection found the fields missing from required schema and DIRECTOR_LOCK_FIELDS before the patch.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The fields were present but digest validation ignored them.
hypotheses.verification: DIRECTOR_LOCK_FIELDS governed digest comparison, so missing entries there made the digest contract incomplete.

root_cause.semantic_trace: brief.schema.json, director brief template, DIRECTOR_LOCK_FIELDS, and contracts/standard-chain.yaml are all read by product artifact gates and downstream validators.
root_cause.cause: Director-owned WHY fields were not treated as one contract surface across schema, template, digest lock, and chain declaration.

issues.fix: Added Director WHY fields to canonical schema required/properties, templates authoritative_fields and locked_fields, DIRECTOR_LOCK_FIELDS, standard-chain key_fields, and affected fixtures with recomputed digests.

four_questions.root_cause: Contract surfaces drifted across canonical schema, template, validator, and chain declaration.
four_questions.fix_complete: Yes. Both machine validation and sample artifacts now cover the same Director field set.
four_questions.new_risk: Digest churn across sample artifacts; mitigated by replay oracle regeneration and canonical validation tests.

issues.symptom: Manager UNIT Integration Context, Verification Plan, structured AC, and design decisions were absent from unit-definition canonical truth.

hypotheses.hypothesis: unit-definition schema remained on the old minimal field set.
hypotheses.verification: Schema inspection showed old authoritative fields before the regression test failed.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Only templates were stale while validators already enforced the fields.
hypotheses.verification: validate_product_closure.py did not enforce integration_context or verification_plan before the patch.

root_cause.semantic_trace: Product Manager writes UNIT JSON, design/test-design/tech-lead consume UNIT JSON through unit-definition schema and validate_product_closure.
root_cause.cause: UNIT capability additions were documented in skill prose but not promoted into canonical UNIT contract and validators.

issues.fix: Added integration_context, structured acceptance_criteria objects, verification_plan, and design_decision_candidates to schema/template/standard-chain/validator and updated pilot fixtures.

four_questions.root_cause: Canonical UNIT schema and validator did not encode the newer Manager handoff semantics.
four_questions.fix_complete: Yes. Required fields, structured AC item requirements, template authoritative fields, chain key_fields, and runtime validation now align.
four_questions.new_risk: Existing UNIT fixtures needed migration; mitigated by updating all standard-chain sample and pilot UNIT fixtures.
four_questions.test_coverage: tests/test-product-artifact-contract.sh and tests/test-standard-chain-foundation-registry.sh cover the new UNIT truth.

issues.symptom: phase-prd output-contract promised business_flows, user_paths, rule_mappings, and design_decision_candidates without canonical phase-prd fields.

hypotheses.hypothesis: phase-prd canonical template had not been updated.
hypotheses.verification: Template and schema inspection showed missing Manager phase fields before RED failure.
output-contract described phase-prd.json itself as the output location, not a projection.

root_cause.semantic_trace: phase-prd schema and template define Product Manager handoff truth; standard-chain declares the same artifact for downstream consumers.
root_cause.cause: Manager output contract and canonical phase-prd truth had divergent field sets.

issues.fix: Added phase business semantics to phase-prd schema/template, standard-chain key_fields, closure validation, and all pilot phase-prd fixtures.

four_questions.root_cause: Manager output prose advanced ahead of canonical fields.
four_questions.fix_complete: Yes. The fields are now represented in schema, template, chain declaration, fixtures, and validator checks.
four_questions.new_risk: Replay fixture digests changed; mitigated by regenerating replay oracles.
four_questions.test_coverage: tests/test-product-artifact-contract.sh and pilot replay tests assert the new field surface.

issues.symptom: design could start with brief/phase/unit files present even if Product Manager handoff was not confirmed or issue ledgers were not closed.

hypotheses.hypothesis: design completion gate lacked a product closure validation call.
hypotheses.verification: shared/skills/design/scripts/completion_check.sh did not call validate_product_closure.py before the patch.

hypotheses.hypothesis: design SKILL.md documented a gate that the script forgot.
hypotheses.verification: design SKILL.md only required artifacts to exist and treated missing review_conclusion as a warning before the patch.

root_cause.semantic_trace: design SKILL.md preconditions and completion_check.sh are the entry and gate for downstream design work.
root_cause.cause: Design handoff readiness was described too weakly and not connected to canonical product closure validation.

issues.fix: Updated design preconditions and completion_check.sh to require product closure validation, delivery_confirmation.status=confirmed, and closed review_conclusion/issue_ledger.

four_questions.root_cause: Design gate checked artifact presence instead of canonical closure state.
four_questions.fix_complete: Yes. The script now invokes validate_product_closure.py for brief and phase-prd before design artifact validation.
four_questions.new_risk: Stricter gate may fail incomplete handoffs earlier; this is intended fail-closed behavior.

issues.symptom: Lifecycle retain decisions could pass with non-empty evidence_refs but without measured fidelity/uplift thresholds.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The lifecycle framework validated only enum values and evidence presence.
hypotheses.verification: tests/test-skill-lifecycle-eval-framework.sh lacked retain metric checks before RED.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Retain metric enforcement existed in eval fixtures instead of the test.
hypotheses.verification: The test did not read threshold fields for retain decisions before the patch.

root_cause.semantic_trace: The lifecycle eval framework is the gate that accepts or rejects lifecycle-review.json decisions.
root_cause.cause: The test accepted retain decisions without binding them to empirical measurement completion and thresholds.

issues.fix: Added retain checks requiring completed encoded_preference measurement_status, fidelity >= 0.80, and positive capability uplift measured_delta.

four_questions.root_cause: Retain decision validation was too shallow.
four_questions.fix_complete: Yes. Retain now needs empirical evidence instead of evidence_refs alone.
four_questions.new_risk: Legacy skills with unfinished retain measurements will fail, which matches the review requirement.
four_questions.test_coverage: tests/test-skill-lifecycle-eval-framework.sh now covers retain thresholds with synthetic pass and failure fixtures.

issues.symptom: Product Manager eval anchors PA-4, PA-5, and PA-6 were not consumed by eval scenarios.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Anchors existed but were not mapped into eval cases.
hypotheses.verification: Anchor-to-case scan in lifecycle framework failed on unused PA-4/PA-5/PA-6 before the patch.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The anchors were intentionally informational and should not be hard coverage.
hypotheses.verification: The finding identified them as critical preferences for review closure, Director lock digest, and delivery confirmation.

root_cause.semantic_trace: The lifecycle framework reads eval scenarios and preference anchors from product-manager/evals/evals.json.
root_cause.cause: Preference anchors were maintained separately from scenario coverage.

issues.fix: Mapped PA-4 and PA-6 into canonical-review-required, PA-5 into Director-lock scenarios, added unit-context-and-ac-closure, and added unused-anchor validation for product skills.

four_questions.root_cause: Eval anchor coverage was not machine-enforced.
four_questions.fix_complete: Yes. Product skills now fail if anchors are unused by scenarios.
four_questions.new_risk: Future product anchors require scenario mapping, which is intended.

issues.symptom: Context budget allowlist expires=2026-05-15 was printed but not parsed, so expired exceptions would remain WARN_ALLOWED.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The script had no date parser or comparison.
hypotheses.verification: CODEX_CONTEXT_BUDGET_TODAY=2026-05-16 test initially failed because the script exited 0.
tests/test-skill-context-budget.sh contained only local WARN_ALLOWED printing before the patch.

root_cause.semantic_trace: run-all invokes tests/test-skill-context-budget.sh; the new expiry regression test drives it with CODEX_CONTEXT_BUDGET_TODAY.
root_cause.cause: Allowlist metadata was treated as display text rather than a gate condition.

issues.fix: Parsed expires=YYYY-MM-DD, compared it with CODEX_CONTEXT_BUDGET_TODAY or current date, and added an expiry regression test to run-all.

four_questions.root_cause: Expiry metadata had no enforcement path.
four_questions.fix_complete: Yes. Expired allowlist entries now fail closed.
four_questions.new_risk: Expired allowlist will fail CI after 2026-05-15; that is the desired follow-up trigger.
four_questions.test_coverage: tests/test-skill-context-budget-expiry.sh verifies the post-expiry failure path.
